title: 小重山（昨夜寒蛩不住鸣）
author: 岳飞
intro: The quiet side of a war hero. Woken at midnight by crickets, a general paces the steps under a hazy moon, his hair gone white and his homeland still lost — and wonders who would listen if he played his heart out on the zither.
analysis: 如果说《满江红》是大声呐喊，这首《小重山》就是深夜里的低声叹息。上阕：秋夜，蟋蟀叫个不停，把作者从千里之外的梦中惊醒——梦里也许正在北方作战，也许回到了故乡。已经三更了，他一个人起来绕着台阶走；四周很安静，帘外的月亮朦朦胧胧。下阕说出心事：为了功名事业，头发都白了；故乡山上的松竹都已老去，却被战事阻住，回不去。想把满腹心事弹给瑶琴听，可是懂我的人太少，就算琴弦弹断了，又有谁听呢？这里用了伯牙和钟子期“知音”的典故：钟子期死后，伯牙摔琴断弦，不再弹琴。一般认为岳飞在抗金和朝廷主和之间受到压制，这首词写的就是这种孤独。
analysisEn: If “The River All Red” is a battle cry, this lyric is a sigh in the middle of the night. In the first half, autumn crickets chirp without stopping and wake the speaker from a dream of somewhere a thousand miles away — perhaps the northern front, perhaps home. It is already the third watch, around midnight. He gets up and walks alone around the steps. Everyone else is asleep, and beyond the curtain the moon is hazy. The second half tells us what is on his mind. He has gone white-haired chasing a great cause; the pines and bamboos on the hills of home have grown old, and the war blocks his way back. He would like to pour his feelings into the zither, but there are few who truly understand, and if the strings snapped, who would even hear? This alludes to a famous story: the musician Bo Ya had one friend, Zhong Ziqi, who understood his music perfectly. When Zhong died, Bo Ya broke his zither and never played again. Zhī yīn (“one who knows the tone”) still means a true friend in Chinese. Readers usually connect the poem to Yue Fei’s frustration with a court that preferred peace talks to his campaigns.
background: Yue Fei (1103–1142) was a Southern Song general who fought the Jin for most of his life. The court, led by the chief minister Qin Hui, sought peace and recalled him; he was imprisoned and executed. This lyric is traditionally dated to his last years, when his campaigns were being held back.
pronunciation: 小重山 chóng；寒蛩 qióng（蟋蟀）；三更 gēng；绕阶行 xíng；为功名 wèi；将 jiāng；知音少 shǎo；谁 shuí（诗词中通常读 shuí）。“人悄悄”按现代词典读 qiāo qiāo（安静无声）；部分注本读 qiǎo qiǎo。
version: 采用通行文本，全词上下两阕。“瑶琴”一本作“瑶筝”（《藏一话腴》），通行本作“瑶琴”。

lines.py: zuó yè hán qióng bù zhù míng
lines.lit: Last night the cold crickets chirped without stopping.
lines.en: All last night the autumn crickets would not stop.

lines.py: jīng huí qiān lǐ mèng, yǐ sān gēng
lines.lit: Startled back from a dream a thousand li away — already the third watch.
lines.en: They broke a dream of a place a thousand miles off. Midnight already.

lines.py: qǐ lái dú zì rào jiē xíng
lines.lit: I get up and walk alone around the steps.
lines.en: I rise and pace the steps alone.

lines.py: rén qiāo qiāo, lián wài yuè lóng míng
lines.lit: People are silent; outside the curtain the moon is hazy-bright.
lines.en: No one stirs. Beyond the curtain, a blurred moon.

lines.lit: White-headed, for the sake of merit and fame.
lines.en: My hair has gone white in the service of my cause.

lines.py: jiù shān sōng zhú lǎo, zǔ guī chéng
lines.lit: On the old hills the pines and bamboos are old; my homeward road is blocked.
lines.en: Pines and bamboo on the hills of home grow old, and still the road back is closed.

lines.py: yù jiāng xīn shì fù yáo qín
lines.lit: I want to entrust my feelings to the jade zither.
lines.en: I would tell my heart to the zither —

lines.py: zhī yīn shǎo, xián duàn yǒu shuí tīng
lines.lit: Those who know the tune are few; if the strings break, who will listen?
lines.en: but few understand the music. If the strings broke, who would hear?

words.note: 蛩：蟋蟀，现代汉语说“蟋蟀”“蛐蛐儿”。
现代汉语仍用，如“不住地点头”。
古代把夜晚分为五更；今天还说“半夜三更”。
现代汉语“悄悄地”多指不出声地做事。
首：头。现代汉语“白头偕老”。

words.en: one who understands you; a true friend
words.note: 出自伯牙、钟子期的故事；今天仍常用。

imagery.name: 蛩
imagery.zh: 秋夜蟋蟀不停地叫，把人惊醒，也让夜更显得冷清。
imagery.en: Crickets chirping through the autumn night wake him and make the dark feel colder and emptier.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 朦胧的月色就像他看不清的前途和压在心上的愁。
imagery.en: The hazy moon is like his clouded future and the weight on his mind.

imagery.name: 松
imagery.zh: 故乡山上的松树老了，说明离家太久。
imagery.en: The pines on the hills of home have grown old: he has been away too long.

imagery.name: 竹
imagery.zh: 和松一起代表故乡，也暗示他坚贞的品格。
imagery.en: With the pines, bamboo stands for home — and quietly for his own steadfast character.

imagery.name: 琴
imagery.zh: 想对琴倾诉，却没有知音，写出不被理解的孤独。
imagery.en: He would pour his heart into the zither, but no one understands — the loneliness of being unheard.
